title: ProTrain Match — Visual Research & Art Direction
status: Research proposal — awaiting Imran's selection; no ad production authorized by this report
method: Opened actual Behance project pages in the browser, checked visible title/owner, inspected campaign compositions beyond covers, and saved selected project images through the browser page-assets capability. Selection is based on transferable principles and ProTrain fit, not appreciation counts. Typeface identities and exact reference HEX values are not inferred from appearances. Conversion relevance is art-direction judgment, not measured performance.

references.title: Study Abroad - Social Media Creative Ads Design
references.style: Photographic education posters: architectural cutouts, students, restrained paper treatments, and distinct destination modules.
references.typography: Large destination or qualification headline above grouped details; sans-serif and condensed display forms. Font families unverified. The page's presentation montage is not a single ad.
references.color: Light neutral and pale blue/pink fields, dark green panels, and localized orange/red highlights. Borrow the limited roles, not these exact colors.
references.strength: A recognisable subject and a strong first read survive changes in imagery. Consistent brand/footer anchors hold different compositions together.
references.weakness: Logo arrays, small requirements, QR codes, flags and contact strips compete at feed size. Destination imagery can imply an agency service rather than academic matching.
references.adapt: Give Campus France one clear headline zone and group illustrative choices tightly. Replace destination spectacle with the actual academic decision. Do not import institutional logos, offers or claims.
references.conversion: Fast topic recognition can qualify attention. A clearer next action could support entry into Match; the reference provides no evidence of paid-report conversion.
references.scope: Cover, campaign montage and poster compositions inspected; selected montage saved. Useful for hierarchy, not proof or claims.

references.title: Social Media - SaaS
references.designer: Eduardo Richter and José Felipe Mondadori
references.focus: Keep the pain and product connected
references.style: Billnest campaign combining typographic messages, human imagery, flat illustration and small invoice-status motifs.
references.typography: Conversational question first, short product explanation second; common logo and palette across different compositions. Clean sans-serif forms; font family unverified.
references.color: White, near-black plum and saturated violet. Violet-on-dark sections are less legible than white-on-dark sections.
references.strength: The campaign varies the visual while preserving an identifiable brand. Small invoice events connect abstract automation to a concrete task.
references.weakness: Some long hooks, dense support and decorative swashes weaken the first read. A generic laptop portrait alone does not prove the mechanism.
references.adapt: Keep one academic problem, one product explanation and one action. Use a compact, genuine report detail or a labelled educational relationship instead of decorative UI. Recolor to ProTrain's documented palette.
references.conversion: Task-specific language helps explain why a SaaS product matters. For Match, the equivalent is understanding why a formation fits, not an unsupported promise of admission.
references.scope: Cover and nine-post campaign grid inspected; two individual source posters saved. No product-performance data verified.

references.title: Tecnologia & Software | Social Media
references.focus: Give every post a dominant message
references.style: Nexustech editorial technology system: dark fields, oversized type, luminous green structures, 3D objects and alternate typographic compositions.
references.typography: An oversized headline is anchored to one side with subordinate explanation and a compact CTA. The wider grid changes scale while repeating small brand anchors. Font family unverified.
references.color: Near-black, white and bright green. Gradients and glossy objects create a technology mood rather than product evidence.
references.strength: Strong light/dark hierarchy, a coherent campaign rhythm, and typography that can lead without relying on a face.
references.weakness: Reflective abstract objects do not explain a product. Saturated green and small peripheral text can overwhelm; displayed percentages are not evidence for ProTrain.
references.adapt: Borrow the single-message discipline, alignment and quiet brand anchors. Use ProTrain forest and ivory, reserve amber for action, and replace chrome objects with meaningful choices or genuine evidence.
references.conversion: Distinct hierarchy can make the hook and action easier to find. Generic technology spectacle would weaken Match's explanation and should not be carried across.
references.scope: Cover, case-study text and multi-post campaign grid inspected; two individual posters saved. Publication date requires page recheck; not used to rank the work.

references.title: Social Media Visuals for Education Brands
references.style: A clean blue education poster with a compact information panel, a pointing student and generous separation between headline and supporting content.
references.typography: The destination is the largest line; the information panel creates a second reading stop. Script decoration is secondary. Typeface families unverified.
references.color: Deep blue content field, lighter blue surround, white type and a white information panel. A restrained palette gives the panel a clear role.
references.strength: A person's gesture directs attention to specific information. The panel gives supporting content its own contrast and breathing room.
references.weakness: The student still occupies substantial space. The action is small, and contact placeholders show a portfolio presentation rather than demonstrated live advertising.
references.adapt: Use alignment or gaze to connect the existing student with the academic choices. Give the supporting message a high-contrast, readable area. Keep both visible at phone size.
references.conversion: Findable explanatory content can help the viewer understand the next step. The small reference CTA is a limitation to correct, not a conversion pattern to repeat.
references.scope: Flat poster and Instagram/device presentations inspected. The repeated mockups show one core design, not a broad campaign system.

references.title: Design Studio | Creative Learning Campaign
references.style: White space, black-and-white cutout photography, black typography and a single acid-green highlight; layouts adapt into carousel and device presentations.
references.typography: Short stacked phrases mix light and heavy sans-serif weights. One highlighted word creates emphasis; the same text modules rearrange across formats. Font family unverified.
references.color: Black, white, grey and electric lime. The system is memorable with very few color roles.
references.strength: A headline can dominate without a large photographic background. The repeated type relationship remains recognisable across layouts.
references.weakness: The stripe across the eyes, arrows and loose circles add decoration. Generic learning language and the passive presenter do not demonstrate a specific service.
references.adapt: Borrow weight contrast, short fixed lines and a single purposeful emphasis. Keep ProTrain colors and the existing active scene; avoid eye bars, slanted Arabic, decorative arrows and broken Arabic word styling.
references.conversion: A short typographic first read may improve comprehension in a feed. It still needs a specific mechanism or evidence to justify a paid report.
references.scope: Poster mockup, carousel arrangements and laptop/mobile presentations inspected. These are variations of one campaign message.

references.title: Study Abroad Academy | Branding & Social Media
references.focus: Keep identity stable as compositions change
references.style: KAB brand case study extending from palette and typography to print, website and a varied social campaign. Aspirational student/country composites share a consistent frame.
references.typography: The identity boards explicitly name Montserrat and Cairo. Social posts use large destination or question headlines and repeat a small top brand mark. This does not validate mixed-script ProTrain line order.
references.color: Deep blue and yellow lead, with supporting green/cyan documented in the case study. Social posts repeat blue/yellow and white framing.
references.strength: Brand position, a limited palette and framing provide continuity without requiring an identical photo position on every post.
references.weakness: Landmarks, planes and passive stock students make the work agency-like. Thin branding and long country names lose clarity when reduced; benefit lists become small.
references.adapt: Define a stable corporate-logo/Match anchor, color roles and type pairing, then vary the composition by angle. Use ProTrain's supplied logo and Cairo/Poppins, not KAB artwork or its destination template.
references.conversion: Campaign recognition can support continuity across exposures. Recognition alone does not establish trust, matching quality or purchases.
references.scope: Identity/color/type boards, print/web applications and social campaign inspected. This is a system reference rather than a model for direct-response proof.

screened_out.title: Creative EdTech Social Media Post
screened_out.designer: Visual Graphics, SOYOD AHMOD, Kamil Ahmod, Guru's Agency and Billal Hossen
screened_out.reason: Inspected the actual post grid. Dense neon treatments and many text tiers conflict with the current clarity brief. Descriptive claims about calm palettes and conversion were not accepted as visual or performance evidence.

screened_out.title: Study Abroad Social Media Post Design
screened_out.reason: Inspected the destination posters and grid. Dense benefit/contact strips and a visible visa-success claim are poor patterns for Match's evidence and no-guarantee constraints.

screened_out.title: UK University Admission Campaign – Social Media Design
screened_out.reason: Actual project verified and opening admission composition inspected. The celebratory graduate/landmark scene and generic announcement do not explain academic matching; not selected.

screened_out.title: Social Media Post Design | Educational Consultancy
screened_out.reason: Inspected flat posters and phone presentation. Rejection-led country messaging, landmarks and dense footer contact details are less useful for the personalized-report decision.

screened_out.title: Social Media Design l Hangug
screened_out.reason: Opened from an EdTech search result, then verified the case study identifies a Korean street-food brand. Excluded as a category mismatch. Search placement was not treated as subject verification.
